entry.title: GitHub Code Quality Findings REST API [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now access GitHub Code Quality findings programmatically through a REST API, giving you the same visibility in your own tools that you already have in the GitHub UI. Use these endpoints to pull CodeQL findings into dashboards, ticketing systems, or automated remediation workflows without manual exports. This makes it easier to track code quality at scale and integrate security data into the processes your team already uses.

Expected Outcome

Developers and security teams gain a reliable, scriptable way to consume code quality data from GitHub, enabling richer integrations and faster response to findings. By exposing findings through a standard REST API, teams can build agentic workflows and custom tooling that act on results automatically—reducing the manual effort required to manage and remediate code quality issues across repositories.

entry.title: Self-Hosted Runner Peak Concurrency Visibility for Administrators [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Administrators can now easily see the highest number of self-hosted runner jobs running at the same time across their organization or enterprise, all in one place. This helps teams understand their usage and estimate future costs before new pricing takes effect.

Expected Outcome

By providing clear visibility into peak self-hosted runner concurrency, admins can confidently plan budgets, avoid surprise charges, and ensure a smooth transition to the upcoming pricing model. This change empowers organizations to make informed decisions and manage their GitHub Actions resources more effectively.

entry.title: npm package ecosystems now use Dependabot to generate dependency graphs [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

npm package ecosystems now use Dependabot to generate dependency graphs, replacing the previous static parsing mechanism. This means customers benefit from full transitive dependency coverage, accurate "dev dependency" labeling, and the ability to access npm packages in private registries through org-wide Dependabot secret configurations. Because the parser is part of the open-source dependabot-core community, customers also gain transparency into how their dependencies are resolved.

Expected Outcome

By unifying npm dependency graph generation onto Dependabot's pipeline, we deliver a more accurate, complete, and configurable dependency analysis experience. Customers will see richer dependency graphs that include transitive dependencies and proper dev/production classification — improving their ability to assess supply chain risk. This also eliminates friction for teams using private npm registries, since existing Dependabot secret configurations now apply automatically.

entry.title: One-click GitHub Pages deployments [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Getting a site live on GitHub Pages no longer requires CI/CD expertise. One-click GitHub Pages deployments give you a guided, single-action path from repository to published site—no manual workflow authoring, no YAML debugging, no guesswork. Pages automatically detects your framework (e.g., Next.js, Vite) and walks you through a streamlined deploy flow, so you spend less time on infrastructure and more time shipping. This brings the GitHub Pages experience in line with modern "connect and deploy" expectations, making it the easiest way to publish directly from your repo.

Expected Outcome

We want to dramatically reduce time-to-first-deploy for GitHub Pages, eliminating the setup friction that has historically pushed users toward third-party hosting providers. By lowering the barrier from multi-step Actions configuration to a single guided action, we expect more repositories to adopt Pages as their default publishing target, fewer failed first deployments, and higher retention among users who would otherwise abandon the setup process. Ultimately, Pages becomes a viable, competitive default for any repository that needs a published site—across Free, Team, and Cloud plans.

entry.title: Actions Debugger [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The Actions Debugger gives developers an interactive way to troubleshoot GitHub Actions workflows in real time, so you can spend less time guessing and more time building. Securely attach to a running job during execution, inspect environment variables, filesystem state, and step outputs with a debug client of your choice, and re-run individual steps without restarting the entire workflow.

Expected Outcome

By making debugging interactive and efficient, we aim to shorten feedback cycles and reduce the guesswork involved in fixing workflow problems. Developers will be able to quickly validate assumptions, understand failures, and resolve issues, leading to smoother CI/CD workflows and a better overall experience with GitHub Actions.

entry.title: Dependabot version update support for Deno projects [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Teams building with Deno can now keep their dependencies up to date automatically through Dependabot version updates—without leaving GitHub. Deno's adoption continues to grow, and developers using it deserve the same first-class dependency management experience that npm, pip, and other ecosystems already enjoy. By extending Dependabot to support Deno, we remove a manual maintenance burden and help customers stay secure and current with minimal effort.

Expected Outcome

With this release, Dependabot will automatically detect outdated dependencies in Deno projects and open pull requests to update them. We expect this to reduce the time developers spend manually tracking and updating Deno dependencies, increase the share of Deno projects with up-to-date dependency graphs, and close a gap that has driven customer feedback requesting parity with other supported ecosystems. This is available on GitHub.com (Free, Teams, and Enterprise plans) and GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22+.

entry.title: Workflow Execution Protections: Actor and Event Configuration [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Workflow Execution Protections give you fine-grained control over which GitHub Actions workflows are allowed to run—and who can trigger them. Using an allow-list approach built into repository rulesets, administrators can define trusted actors (specific users, roles, or apps like Dependabot and Copilot) and permitted events (such as push, pull_request, or workflow_dispatch). This means your organization can enforce consistent, centralized security policies across all repositories without relying on ad hoc, per-workflow configurations—reducing your attack surface and scaling governance as you grow.

Expected Outcome

Today, workflows execute based on the workflow file present in the triggering commit, which means anyone with write access could inject malicious changes that run in CI. Workflow Execution Protections close this gap by evaluating enforcement rules before execution begins, blocking unauthorized actors and unexpected event triggers at the gate. The result: stronger supply-chain security, reduced risk of secrets exfiltration, and confidence that only trusted people and automation can initiate workflow runs—whether you're an enterprise managing hundreds of repositories or an open-source maintainer protecting your project from malicious contributions.

entry.title: GHES 3.20 GA
entry.content:
Value Prop

This release is our quarterly update to GitHub Enterprise Server. With it, will come a host of improvements that are tagged with the label "GHES 3.20" on our public roadmap.

Expected Outcome

In every quarterly GHES release, we add a host of capabilities aimed at improving the overall experience for all different types of GitHub Enterprise Server users. As an operator, you can configure a dedicated disk for logs, and use a managed, built-in backup service that does not require a separate host. As a developer, you can experience the improved merge experience on the pull request page. This is designed to help you better understand the state of your pull request and get it merged faster. As an enterprise owner, you can create and manage enterprise teams to simplify governance across their enterprise.

entry.title: GitHub Education's Bulk Academic Verification: Mass Onboarding Tool for Students
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Education’s Bulk Academic Verification helps schools and education partners quickly grant eligible students access to GitHub’s student benefits at scale—without each student needing to complete a separate verification. By streamlining verification for groups (like classes, cohorts, or event attendees), it reduces administrative overhead and helps educators confidently roll out GitHub tooling as part of their curriculum or program.

Expected Outcome

Educators and program organizers can onboard students faster and more reliably, ensuring learners have access to the Student Developer Pack and related GitHub capabilities from day one. This should reduce delays caused by individual verification steps, improve the student setup experience, and make it easier for institutions to integrate GitHub into classrooms, workshops, and training programs.

entry.title: New repository settings to disable or restrict pull requests
entry.content:
Value Prop

Repository maintainers get two new, first-party controls to manage contributions at the repo level: disable pull requests entirely or restrict PR creation to collaborators only. This lets teams share code publicly (or mirror it) without taking on the overhead and risk of unsolicited or low-quality PR submissions, and without needing custom bots or manual triage.

Expected Outcome

Maintainers can reduce PR noise and moderation workload, while still keeping repositories accessible for viewing and forking with clear UX signals about contribution limits. Teams that want controlled contributions can allow PRs from trusted collaborators only, leading to higher-signal contribution flows, fewer unwanted PRs, and smoother maintenance—especially during pauses, release gaps, or in mirrored/readonly repos.

entry.title: IP allow list coverage extended to EMU namespaces [Public preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users (EMUs) will be able to enable the ability for GitHub’s native IP allow list configuration to cover user namespaces. EMUs allow the enterprise to own the user accounts within their enterprise. As an extension to that, enterprises often want all repositories to adhere to their enterprise’s network access policies, including those owned by the user namespace associated to their EMUs.

Expected Outcome

This feature will provide a more secure posture for GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users (EMUs) by limiting access to enterprise-managed user namespaces to the owning enterprise’s IP allow list.

entry.title: OIDC custom properties as claims
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Actions OIDC now supports custom repository properties as claims, enabling platform and security teams to embed rich metadata directly into every token issued from a repository. This structured identity context allows cloud providers, artifact registries, and secrets brokers to enforce attribute-based access control (ABAC) without any workflow-level configuration changes.

Expected Outcome

Teams can expect to eliminate hard-coded allow lists and manual policy exceptions. Replacing them with version controlled repository attributes that automatically propagate into cloud IAM trust policies at scale. Organizations will achieve least-privilege access across hundreds or thousands of repositories with a one-time policy investment, reducing operational burden and improving auditability across every workflow run.

entry.title: Managing low quality issue comments
entry.content:
Value Prop

Managing low-quality issue comments helps teams keep issue conversations focused by nudging users away from short, repetitive replies (like “+1” or “same here”). This makes it easier to scan an issue and quickly find the updates or details that matter most.

Expected Outcome

Repositories should see less comment noise in long-running issues, improving readability and reducing time spent searching for meaningful context. Teams can triage and collaborate more efficiently with clearer threads.

entry.title: Pinned comments on issues
entry.content:
Value Prop

Pinned comments on issues let teams highlight the most important context at the top of an issue, such as workarounds, status updates, decisions, or next steps, so it’s easy to find at a glance. This helps users stay aligned without having to scan long comment threads to locate key information.

Expected Outcome

Teams can reduce time spent searching for key details and keep issues focused by making key information for an issue immediately visible. This will result in fewer repeated questions on an issue and more focused conversations.

entry.title: GitHub Mobile: Repository Creation
entry.content:
Value Prop

Enable first-class repository creation in GitHub Mobile, allowing users to create user-owned new repositories directly from the app.

Expected Outcome

Close the gap by adding native repository creation to GitHub Mobile. This will cover the essential steps to create a user-owned repo, making it easier for users to start a new project on mobile and kick off agentic workflows faster.

entry.title: GitHub Mobile: Coding Agent Live Activities/Notifications
entry.content:
Value Prop

We are introducing a Live Activities widget on GitHub Mobile iOS and Live Update Notifications on GitHub Mobile Android that allows users to monitor the real-time progress of coding agent sessions initiated on both GitHub.com and Mobile.

Expected Outcome

Deliver a seamless, real-time mobile experience for tracking the status and progress of coding agent tasks, enabling users to stay informed and engaged even when away from their desktop.

entry.title: Dependabot alerts assignees
entry.content:
Value Prop

Dependabot alert assignees bring clear ownership and accountability directly to each Dependabot alert, making it easy for security and engineering teams to route work to the right person and track progress at alert-level granularity. By aligning Dependabot with the existing assignee patterns customers already use for code scanning and secret scanning—and supporting autofix workflows, including Copilot coding agent opening draft PRs—teams can standardize how they triage and remediate vulnerabilities across all GitHub security signals.

Expected Outcome

With alert assignees in place, customers can expect faster and more consistent vulnerability remediation because every alert has an explicit owner, clearer prioritization, and fewer “orphaned” findings. Large orgs should see reduced alert fatigue, improved coordination between AppSec and development teams, and better ability to drive “get clean / stay clean” programs by measuring and managing remediation at scale across repositories and portfolios.

entry.title: Dependabot detection of malware packages for npm
entry.content:
Value Prop

Dependabot malware alerts help you proactively identify when your repositories pull in known malicious package versions (starting with npm and expanding as coverage grows), so you’re not relying on manual threat intel gathering or piecing together signals across multiple tools. By surfacing targeted supply-chain malware risk directly where you manage dependencies, teams can quickly understand exposure and take action before a malicious package spreads further in their environments.

Expected Outcome

With malware alerts, customers can expect faster detection and response to malicious dependency incidents across large repo portfolios, with clearer notification and prioritization of the highest-risk packages. This reduces time spent on investigation, lowers the likelihood of shipping compromised code, and strengthens overall software supply chain trust without requiring additional tooling or custom monitoring.

entry.title: Saved views on the repository Issues page
entry.content:
Value Prop

Saved views on the repository Issues page let teams create and share custom views directly within a repository. This makes it easier to manage workflows and makes common sets of issues organized and consistently accessible for everyone, such as items that need to be triaged or high priority bugs.

Expected Outcome

Teams can align on a standard set of custom views to reduce time spent recreating filters, switching contexts, and managing bookmarks, and makes ongoing triage and prioritization more consistent.

entry.title: New global PR /pulls experience (M3)
entry.content:
Value Prop

The new global Pull Requests experience on github.com/pulls provides a redesigned, high-performance hub for developers to view and manage all of their pull requests across GitHub in one place. With enhanced search and filtering and customizable saved views, developers can quickly find what matters most and stay on top of their code review workflows.

Expected Outcome

With the new /pulls experience, developers can expect to spend less time searching for relevant pull requests and more time shipping code. Saved views enable developers to tailor the experience to their unique workflows and preferences, while improved performance and a modern UI reduce context-switching and accelerate review cycles.
